title: camera_layout
description:
Robot -> client. How to slice the single composited video track.

The robot encodes ALL of its cameras into one H.264 track (one encode is the only affordable choice on a Pi 5 with no hardware encoder), tiled left-to-right then top-to-bottom in `tiles` order. This frame is the ONLY authoritative description of that tiling -- in particular it is NOT derived from ack.descriptor.cameras, which is diagnostic metadata. A mock that generates its layout from the descriptor will hide real layout bugs.

Repeated several times on channel open because the control channel is unreliable; repeats are idempotent and carry identical content. A robot with a single camera sends NO layout at all: absence means the whole frame is that one camera.

A layout with empty `tiles` is INVALID per this schema. A client that receives one must reject it and KEEP any layout it already had -- never adopt it -- because one malformed repeat would otherwise blank the grid for the rest of the session.

tiles.description: Camera role per tile, in row-major order. Length should be <= cols*rows; trailing grid cells with no tile are blank.
